executive_assessment.text: Santiago/Santo Antão modelled flood exposure, Sal's coastal scenarios and dated São Vicente flood impacts add differentiated island evidence.
Reported emergency water transport, named water-sector pilots and warning-roadmap milestones deepen capacity, with planned actions distinguished from measured outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-01-15 reports: Estimated: 16% exposed to extreme drought, 7% to extreme floods; poor households face 1.4x drought exposure. Drought affects all islands (lower in São Vicente/Sal); 90% of flood exposure is in Santiago/Santo Antão.

Source dated 2025-01-15 reports: The CCDR identifies 143,000 people (28%) in poverty/food-insecurity hotspots; six municipalities have acute food insecurity of at least 15%, five on Santiago and one on Santo Antão.
Source dated 2025-01-15 reports: RCP 8.5 projections raise coastal-flood exposure from 29% of coastal residents now to about 32% by 2050; Sal's exposed urban coast could rise from 33% to over 38%.
Source dated 2025-01-15 reports: The CCDR identifies drought and tourism as rural-to-urban migration drivers, especially toward Sal and Boa Vista.

Source dated 2025-10-22 reports: The IFRC update reports at least 12 deaths, five missing, over 27,500 affected and 1,500 displaced in São Vicente after floods and landslides, with damage to homes, roads, health services, markets and water systems.

Source dated 2025-10-22 reports: By September 2025, the Red Cross had provided household items to 238 households and food to 271 in named São Vicente neighborhoods, and conducted three protection and inclusion trainings for 79 volunteers.
Source dated 2025-10-22 reports: The Red Cross reports ferrying about 150 m³ of drinking water daily from Santo Antão to São Vicente after flooding damaged the local distribution system.

Source dated not stated reports: UNDP's completed-project page describes pilots across three municipalities and five basins, including groundwater intake and drip irrigation in Ribeira Seca and planned reforestation/soil conservation at Planalto Leste on Santo Antão.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 18 of 18 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

No inspected source explicitly links climate hazards to armed conflict or violence in Cabo Verde. The CCDR links drought with rural-to-urban migration, and IFRC reports flood displacement and heightened protection risks, without establishing conflict causation.
The CCDR's municipality food-insecurity categories use island-level poverty data; modeled hazard estimates use different return periods and cited data years.
IFRC flood counts are operation-period estimates; response monitoring was incomplete, and the WMO roadmap was still awaiting validation in its December 2025 update.
UNDP's project summary does not name every municipality or independently quantify the adaptation outcomes of its completed project.
